newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT drops 2.69 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: PLDT drops 2.69 pct in late trade.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co slipped 25 pesos, or 2.69 percent, to 905 pesos in late trade on Monday on profit-taking after it climbed to a two-year high last Friday, brokers said.

"The reason PLDT rose was because its forex earnings would boost its overall bottomline if the peso weakens but the Central Bank is keeping everything steady so those who bought PLDT are now cashing in their gains," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Monday the Central Bank will not allow a devaluation of the peso.
PLDT was the third most heavily traded issue in late trade as turnover reached 84.39 million pesos.
